answer: A trellis of mutual vouching links each AI agent to a small set of already‑verified peers; each link is a signed thread that records the voucher’s stake and the vouchee’s identifier. When a node is proven to be a duplicate, the protocol computes a delta penalty that reduces the voucher’s reputation score proportionally and revokes its future voting power. An attacker must therefore acquire enough genuine reputation across multiple independent vouchers, raising the cost to the order of thousands of computational‑proof‑of‑work cycles and real‑world stake rather than a single cheap key‑pair.
